name: Automatic server backups (rolling slots)
notes: Hetzner prices backups as a percentage of server cost (~20%). 4.49 * 0.20 = 0.898. Enabled via the hcloud_server module's backups_enabled variable.

name: Block volume for the Postgres data directory
notes: Optional at rung 0: data_volume_size_gb defaults to 0, keeping Postgres on a named docker volume on the 40 GB boot disk, which is ample for a ~63 MB compressed dataset. Kept as a separate line because volume storage scales independently of server type -- see hetzner-topology.md rung 1.

name: Offsite nightly pg_dump target (Storage Box or S3-compatible)
notes: Required by the backup task: an on-box backup does not survive the failure mode it exists for. Smallest tier suffices for a ~63 MB compressed nightly dump at local-style retention.

name: Primary IPv4 address
notes: Hetzner bills IPv4 separately from the server. Required: Caddy must answer the ACME HTTP-01 challenge on port 80.

service_display_name: CROSS-PROVIDER COSTS -- not billed by Hetzner, but caused by this deployment

name: Retained image storage from dual-push
notes: Dual-push (GHCR + Artifact Registry) is a permanent decision, not transitional, so AR storage billing continues. Cost grows without bound: sha-tagged images accumulate forever and no retention policy exists. This is one of the two reasons .github/workflows/openthrottle-docker.yml is currently disabled (if: false); the other is the absent build cache. GHCR itself is free for public repositories. Quantify from actual AR storage before re-enabling -- see docs/monorepo/ci-cost.md.

name: Terraform state for the hcloud root
notes: The hcloud environment root reuses the existing versioned state bucket under a distinct key rather than migrating state. A few state files add no measurable cost. Being on GCS does not make a Hetzner deployment a GCP deployment.

service_display_name: METHODOLOGY -- read before extending this file
This is the sibling of gcp-estimate.csv, not its replacement. Both providers stay supported, so both keep a live estimate. See provider-contract.md.

Postgres and Redis have NO line item here, and that is the entire cost story of the Hetzner path: they are containers on the box, not managed services. Do not add rows for them. On the GCP path they are Cloud SQL + Memorystore, which is where that estimate's bulk sits.

Do NOT copy gcp-estimate.csv's methodology. It prices Cloud SQL for MySQL while the stack runs Postgres, so its 52.61 USD total is wrong in kind, not just in degree. Fixing that file is out of scope for this plan but is a known defect (provider-contract.md, 'Known defects on the GCP path').

That 52.61 USD/mo has also never been billed: the GCP application composition is commented out in environments/staging/openthrottle.tf and absent from production and development. It is a projection of what the GCP path would cost if applied.
